q: The electric potentials of charged conductors are expressed relative to the electric potential of the _____.
e: Potential is work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity, V = W/q. The electric potentials of charged conductors are expressed relative to the electric potential of the earth. Sun or moon is not this quantity.

q: The earth is a conductor and is regarded as having _____ electric potential.
e: Potential is work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity, V = W/q. The earth is a conductor and is regarded as having zero electric potential. Do not trade zero for infinite or negative.

q: When a charged conductor is connected to the earth, its electric potential becomes _____.
e: Potential is work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity, V = W/q. When a charged conductor is connected to the earth, its electric potential becomes zero. Maximum or negative is not this quantity.

q: When a positively charged body is connected to the earth, electrons flow from the earth to the _____.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. When a positively charged body is connected to the earth, electrons flow from the earth to the body. Air or insulator is not this quantity.

q: The net charge of the earth does not change when it gains or loses electrons because the number of electrons is very small compared to the _____ of the earth.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. The net charge of the earth does not change when it gains or loses electrons because the number of electrons is very small compared to the size of the earth. Mass or density is not this quantity.

q: When a negatively charged body is connected to the earth, electrons flow from the body to the _____.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. When a negatively charged body is connected to the earth, electrons flow from the body to the earth. Do not trade earth for air or positive plate.
